abstract: Background: Microbiome profiles combine sequence-derived units with taxonomy. Pretrained models use different community vocabularies and are often evaluated on few labels, leaving their value under broad competitive evaluation unclear. We introduce OTU-Taxa, which pairs operational taxonomic unit (OTU) identity with hierarchical taxonomy during autoregressive pretraining on unlabeled profiles. Results: In an in-domain evaluation across 250 Microbe Atlas Project (MAP)-derived classification tasks with disjoint folds, mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.744 for OTU-Taxa and 0.749 for Random Forest. OTU-Taxa was the highest-ranked pretrained method; Nemenyi comparisons did not detect rank differences from Random Forest across the three metrics. The model also generated largely non-copied profiles and recovered more withheld community members at larger cutoffs, while retrieval gave stronger empirical fidelity and early ranking. It also supported abundance-rank readouts and recovered higher-rank classifier assignments from sample context for known-vocabulary OTUs under controlled sequence degradation, although agreement was limited at genus and species ranks. Conclusions: Within the MAP 97% closed-reference 16S vocabulary, the pretrained representation supports in-domain prediction of metadata labels alongside generative and taxonomic readouts. Supervised abundance models, empirical retrieval, and intact-sequence classifiers remain stronger choices for several corresponding endpoints, while OTU-Taxa provides one shared contextual representation across all four analyses.
